# Erdos.p887 — Erdős problem 887

Reference: https://www.erdosproblems.com/887
Imported from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (`ErdosProblems/887.lean`, theorem `erdos_887.parts.ii`, AMS 11).

Is there an absolute constant $K$ such that, for every $C > 0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
$n$ has at most $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$.

## Statement
∃ K, ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    #{ d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋₊ ⌈√n + C * n^((1 : ℝ) / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n } ≤ K

## Strategic notes
Open conjecture — prove-or-refute posture applies to sub-claims,
but the root asserts the conjectured statement itself. No
per-problem hints (benchmark integrity).
